12.3
Εως τίνος
θήσομαι βουλὰς ἐν ψυχῇ μου, ὀδύνας ἐν καρδίᾳ μου ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός;
Τοῦ
αὐτοῦ. ̓Ανθ' ου ὁ Σύμμαχος ἡρμή νευσεν εἰπών· Μέριμναν ἐν τῇ διανοίᾳ μου καθ'
ἡμέραν. Ταῦτα δὲ, φησὶν, ἐγράφη εἰς νουθεσίαν ἡμῶν, ο πως καὶ αὐτοὶ, διαθέσει
τοῦ ταῦτα εἰρηκότος, εἰ γένοιτο ἡμῖν χρεία μετα νοίας καὶ ἐξομολογήσεως ἐπί τισιν
οὐκ ὀρθῶς ἡμῖν πεπραγμένοις, ταῖς αὐταῖς χρησώμεθα μεθόδοις, ω σπερ φαρμάκοις
ψυχῆς σωτηρίοις, εὐκαίρως τοῖς παροῦσι λόγοις τῆς ἐξομολο γήσεως χρώμενοι.
pass_a_gloss: Until what I-will-set counsels in soul of-me, pains in heart of-me of-day and of-night? Of-the same. Instead-of-which the Symmachus interpreted having-said: Care in the mind of-me according-to day. These and, he-says, were-written into admonition of-us, so-that also ourselves, with-disposition of-the these having-said, if there-should-be to-us need of-repentance and of-confession upon some not rightly to-us having-been-done, the same we-might-use methods, as-it-were medicines of-soul saving, timely to-the present words of-the confession using.
pass_b_english: “How long shall I set counsels in my soul, pains in my heart day and night?” (Psalm 12:3).

Of the same. Instead of which Symmachus interpreted saying: “Care in my mind by day.” And these things, he says, were written for our admonition, so that we too, with the disposition of the one who has said these things, if there should be need of repentance and confession for some things not rightly done by us, might use the same methods, as it were saving medicines of the soul, timely using the present words of confession.

choices.why: The psalm-words of confession are medicines, not poisons. Not ‘drugs of the body’.
